sections.heading: What an appraisal includes
sections.html:
Every appraisal is a signed document built from close looking: photographs, fibers and dyes identified, construction and quilting density described, condition reported without flattering anyone, and a value supported by comparable sales.

You leave with the original and I keep a scan on file, which has quietly settled more than one estate conversation and one very stubborn insurance adjuster.

items.quote: The appraisal was accepted without a single question, and the check covered the number on the page.
items.author: An estate attorney

items.quote: She talked me out of washing my grandmother's quilt, and that probably saved it.
items.author: A client from three counties over

sections.heading: How an appointment runs
sections.html:
Bring the quilt folded cloth-to-cloth, in a pillowcase rather than plastic, along with whatever provenance exists: a letter, a label, a memory of whose hope chest it came out of. Provenance does not change the stitching, but it changes the story and sometimes the value.

An appraisal takes about forty-five minutes per quilt. Estate days can be booked by the half day when a whole closet needs documenting at once.

sections.title: About {{guild_name}}
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Certified in 2014, two thousand quilts appraised, and a training that began with my own family's mislabeled heirloom.

sections.heading: Why appraising
sections.html:
My family called ours a Civil War quilt for forty years. The cloth said 1930, the feed sacks said 1938, and the appraisal course said both of those were interesting enough. I took the training to learn the answer and stayed for the quilts other people trust me to read.

Certification is maintained with continuing education every year, and the reference shelf runs from pattern books to auction records. When a quilt deserves a conservator rather than an appraiser, the referral is part of the service.

items.quote: She read the fabric at arm's length and had the decade before she touched it. The room went quiet.
items.author: A county museum curator

sections.title: Questions
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: What a value is based on, whether to wash, and how to store what you cannot bear to use.

items.a: It depends on cloth, condition, construction, and provenance, which is exactly why the written appraisal exists. Guesses do not hold up to an adjuster or an executor.
Almost never before an appraisal. Stains and sizing tell the date story. Bring it as it is; cleaning advice comes with the report.
Acid-free tissue, flat when possible, refolded along new lines a few times a year, and never in plastic or a cedar chest. Both do real damage.
I stabilize and plan; a small circle of conservators and restorers does the fine work. Sometimes the right repair is none at all.
Guild appraisal days happen anywhere five quilts can gather, with travel shared across the bookings.
